sentences.show: Walt Disney wanted his audience to feel like they were standing right next to the conductor.
So he built a new kind of cinema sound.
Fantasia premiered on this day in 1940, in New York.
It was the first commercial film shown in stereo.
33 microphones surrounded the orchestra, and its conductor, Leopold Stokowski.
In the theatre, speakers moved the music across the room. Installing them took a week, around the clock.
It was the same Broadway theatre where Mickey Mouse's Steamboat Willie had played, 12 years before.
Over 1,000 artists drew 500 characters. Mickey got pupils in his eyes, for the first time.
But one sound system cost $85,000. The film flopped.
Its own distributor called it a "long-hair musical".
Today, it is counted among the greatest animated films ever made.
Also on this day: the Holland Tunnel opened, and a solar eclipse darkened Australia.
